key_insight: An input skip can lower VAE reconstruction error without changing the generated distribution, so better reconstruction does not necessarily mean better generation.
engineering_relevance: Evaluate generative quality separately from reconstruction MSE, especially when changing skip strength or observation variance.
method: Derive a Gaussian VAE reparameterization for constant input skip α, with b = 1 − α.
Scale decoder output by b and noise variance by b², preserving the joint distribution while scaling reconstruction MSE by b².
Evaluate separately trained models using energy score and, on known-density Gaussian data, importance-sampled negative log density.
evidence_signal: Gaussian experiments showed lower MSE alongside worse generative scores; seven annual DART records showed mixed skip benefits, while PPCA achieved lower mean energy scores than every neural DART fit.
watch_item: The exact equivalence applies to the specified Gaussian reparameterization; separate training can change generators, and reconstruction-based variance estimation can worsen energy score.
paper_title: An Input Skip Can Reparameterize a VAE Without Improving the Generator
